item.title: AirLink 0.12.0-beta.1
item.description:
# AirLink 0.12.0 Beta 1
AirLink now has a native Qt desktop app for Linux, with macOS and Linux as the main focus of this beta. It sends files and folders directly over the local network, without an account or cloud relay.
## Changes
- Add the Linux desktop, targeting Arch/KDE Plasma under Wayland, with setup, devices, drag-and-drop, transfers/history, Quick Share, clipboard, notifications, tray operation and single-instance handling. - Simplify the macOS recipient view and separate advanced tools. Preserve deliberate setup/settings edits, bind every send to its original recipient/files, show active transfers and at most three recent results per device, and load full history/details in pages. - Introduce independently derived, TLS-bound eight-digit comparison codes with confirmation on both desktops. Existing trusted devices remain saved. Automatic receiving is a separate opt-in for each receiving direction. - Keep control commands responsive during folder preparation; support cancellation, compact summaries and one additional prefetched 8-MiB block per sending slot. Keep TLS, SHA-256, source checks and durable block confirmations. - Provide architecture-specific signed update feeds with the existing Ed25519 key. Automatic notices are optional and limited to once per 24 hours; downloads/installation require a click. Native Linux packages stay under package-manager control. - Correct Windows filesystem/extraction regressions and native installer architecture detection. The Windows app receives the shared protocol, pairing and update improvements.
## Downloads and installation
| System | Choose | | --- | --- | | Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 14+ | `macos-arm64.dmg` | | Intel Mac, macOS 14+ | `macos-x64.dmg` | | Arch x64 | `linux-x64.pkg.tar.zst`, install with `sudo pacman -U ./AirLink-0.12.0-beta.1-linux-x64.pkg.tar.zst` | | Debian 12+ / Ubuntu 24.04+ x64 | `linux-x64.deb` | | Fedora / openSUSE x64 with compatible Qt 6.4+ | `linux-x64.rpm` | | Linux x64 portable or user installation, glibc 2.36+ | `linux-x64.AppImage` | | Windows Intel/AMD | `windows-x64-setup.exe` | | Windows on ARM | `windows-arm64-setup.exe` |
All names begin with `AirLink-0.12.0-beta.1-`. The release includes SHA-256 checksums, the signed release manifest and five signed update feeds. The AppImage bundles Qt plus Wayland/X11 components and offers a user installation with application launcher; native packages use system libraries. The PKGBUILD is in the repository; there is no AUR submission or Linux ARM package.
**macOS is ad hoc signed and not notarized.** A verified download can require first-open approval in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Replace `/Applications/AirLink.app`, keeping only the current app there. Pairings, settings, resumable transfers and received files remain separate. Windows Setup installs under the current user's Programs directory; these betas are not Authenticode signed.
**From 0.11:** manually install the matching 0.12 beta once to adopt the new feeds. Thereafter use Check for Updates in the app/tray menu or Settings → Updates. Use the same beta on both computers to test the new pairing flow. Browser connections retain their separate local-certificate setup.
## Background verification
The candidate is published only after the complete background suites, package lifecycle checks and signature/privacy checks pass. The linked [verification record](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md) gives source revisions, hosted checks and scope; the [Linux package record](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/blob/main/docs/evidence/0.12.0-beta.1-linux-packages.json) pins tested container images.
- Go race tests and vet; 74 Swift tests, 43 Windows Core tests, Qt Core with actual helper subprocesses and 68 web tests. No desktop-controlling tests or application window launches. - Headless native Linux install, synthetic successor upgrade, version ordering, runtime linkage, uninstall and user-data preservation on Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Arch, Fedora 45, openSUSE Leap 16 and Tumbleweed. Windows x64 silent installation, replacement, refusal of a busy/locked app and uninstall; ARM64 payload built and inspected separately. - Repeated same-Mac, two-service TLS comparisons: median 300 MiB 0.935 → 0.785 seconds; 4 GiB 12.907 → 10.206 seconds. Each result has an independent size/hash check. These are local measurements, not WLAN speed claims. - A separate 4-GiB transfer survived pause and abrupt restarts of each service with the final independent hash intact. Simultaneous 300-MiB transfers in both directions passed. Highest sampled RSS in the measured workloads was below 113 MiB per service. - Source/reachable-history and unpacked-package privacy audit, package architecture/license checks, existing-key signatures and verification with the actual Sparkle, NetSparkle and Qt verifiers.
## Known limits and 1.0 gates
This is a beta. Physical Mac↔Arch WLAN, native desktop rendering, Windows ARM64 runtime and a new 100-GB transfer are not proven by these builds/tests. Native interaction and the full device/stability acceptance remain requirements before 1.0.
Many small files remain slow: the 10,000-file control-polling stress case took about 19 minutes on both helpers. No significant improvement is claimed for that workload. Wi-Fi, storage and native-app performance must be measured on the actual devices.
The previous private archive remains private and archived. Existing release tags and application binaries are preserved.
